name: Tempus AI, Inc.

profile.description: Tempus AI is a healthcare technology company applying artificial intelligence to precision medicine, operating two primary segments: Diagnostics ($289.3M Q2 2026 revenue, +20% YoY) and Data & Applications ($93.2M Q2 2026 revenue, +28% YoY). Founded in 2015 by Eric Lefkofsky after his wife's breast cancer diagnosis, the company provides NGS diagnostics, AI-powered clinical decision support, de-identified data licensing to biopharma, and clinical trial matching services. TTM revenue is approximately $1.43B with 21.6% YoY growth, and Q2 2026 marked Tempus's first quarter of net profitability ($5.6M net income) [1][2]. The company announced a $1.5-1.7B acquisition of Personalis expected to close in late 2026 or early 2027 [2].

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Tempus has executed one of healthcare's most impressive growth trajectories, scaling from startup to $1.27B in annual revenue by 2025 while fundamentally changing how oncologists approach treatment decisions. The company built the world's largest library of clinical and molecular data, launched multiple NGS assay products (xT, xR, nP), expanded from oncology into cardiology and neuropsychiatry, and completed the transformative acquisition of Ambry Genetics from Konica Minolta in late 2024, broadening its inherited disease testing capabilities [3][4]. The IPO in June 2024 at approximately $6B valuation, now grown to $12B, validates market confidence. AI Deployment (2/2): Tempus IS an AI company — its entire platform is built on machine learning applied to clinical and molecular data. AI powers diagnostics interpretation, drug target identification, clinical trial matching (Trials platform), and data licensing (Insights product). The Next AI platform and Algos algorithm-based diagnostics generate real revenue across the Diagnostics and Data & Applications segments, totaling $382.5M in Q2 2026 alone [1][2]. Market Share (2/2): Tempus is the leading AI-powered precision medicine platform, named to TIME's 10 Most Influential Health & Life Science Companies of 2026 [3]. The company has strategic collaborations with AstraZeneca, GlaxoSmithKline, Merck, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals, and its Diagnostics segment achieved 31% oncology volume growth YoY in Q2 2026 [2]. No competitor matches Tempus's combination of diagnostic testing, data licensing, and AI-powered clinical decision support at scale. Product Pipeline (1/2): The $1.5-1.7B Personalis acquisition will expand Tempus's capabilities in minimal residual disease (MRD) testing and whole genome sequencing, expected to close late 2026 or early 2027. The company hosted its inaugural Investor Day on May 29, 2026, and guided for $1.595-1.605B in 2026 revenue [2][3]. However, specific next-generation product launches with named timelines beyond the acquisition were not detailed. R&D Intensity (1/1): Tempus invests heavily in R&D relative to its revenue base, developing novel assays, AI algorithms, and data infrastructure. As a pre-profitability company until Q2 2026, the majority of spending has been reinvested into platform development and clinical validation [4].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Tempus was founded by Eric Lefkofsky in 2015 shortly after his wife was diagnosed with breast cancer, giving the company a deeply personal and specific origin story tied to a transformative purpose: using AI to help physicians make better treatment decisions and ultimately defeat disease [3][4]. The mission — making precision medicine accessible and actionable — is distinctive, connects to a larger purpose beyond profit, and has shaped every strategic decision from building the data library to the Ambry acquisition. It falls short of a 4 because the company is only 11 years old and has not yet been tested through a major existential crisis or leadership transition. Community Impact (1/2): Tempus partners with Blood Cancer United to develop a registry for pediatric acute myeloid leukemia, and its precision medicine platform directly serves cancer patients by matching them with targeted therapies and clinical trials [4]. The social value of the business itself is meaningful, though specific charitable giving or community investment programs were not found. Employee Retention (0/2): Tempus has grown rapidly to 3,800 employees but no specific voluntary turnover data, average tenure, or employee satisfaction metrics were found. The company is in a high-growth phase where retention data may not yet be publicly reported. Insider Buying (0/2): CEO Eric Lefkofsky sold 166,250 shares under a pre-arranged Rule 10b5-1 plan in April 2026 at approximately $42/share, netting about $10.5M. While routine for founder-CEOs, this represents net insider selling, not buying [3].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock on available metrics. Tempus's infrastructure profile reflects a high-growth company still transitioning toward profitability. Revenue growth is the standout: YoY growth of 21.6% exceeds the 10% target (score 1.0), and the estimated 5-year CAGR of approximately 45% — from $0.32B in 2022 to $1.43B TTM — massively exceeds the 10% target (score 1.0, 2x weight) [1][2]. However, profitability metrics drag the score: profit margin of -17.8% is below the 0% floor (score 0.0), ROE of -67.4% is deeply negative (score 0.0, 2x weight), reflecting the cumulative losses as the company invested in scaling its platform. D/E of 324.6% exceeds the 300% floor (score 0.0), driven by $1.17B in convertible senior notes as of June 2026 against negative stockholders' equity [5]. Forward P/E and PEG ratio are excluded from scoring as the company has only just reached profitability and forward earnings estimates produce meaningless negative ratios. Cash position of $820.7M at Q2 end provides runway, and the company expects positive cash flow by year-end 2026. Daily dollar volume of $456M provides ample liquidity [1][2].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (9/9): Tempus AI IS the AI infrastructure for precision medicine — the company cannot be disrupted by AI because AI is its entire business model and competitive advantage [2][4]. Every product and service Tempus offers — NGS diagnostics, clinical decision support, data licensing, clinical trial matching, and algorithm-based diagnostics — is built on and powered by AI and machine learning. The company has built the world's largest library of clinical and molecular data, which serves as a proprietary moat that competitors cannot easily replicate. Healthcare AI faces significant regulatory barriers (CLIA, CAP, FDA) that protect established platforms from new entrants. The convergence of AI capability and precision medicine demand creates a structural tailwind for Tempus. The company is at the intersection of two megatrends — AI adoption and personalized healthcare — where each reinforces the other. AI Opportunity (1/1): Tempus generates $1.43B in annual revenue, all of which is AI-driven. The Diagnostics segment ($289.3M Q2 revenue) uses AI for test interpretation and clinical insights, while the Data & Applications segment ($93.2M Q2 revenue) licenses AI-processed data and analytics to biopharma companies [1][2]. Adjusted EBITDA reached $8.0M in Q2 2026, up 244% YoY, with full-year EBITDA guidance of approximately $65M [2].

infinite_game.summary: Tempus AI demonstrates meaningful infinite game characteristics anchored by a deeply personal founding story and a genuine mission to transform healthcare through data and AI. Eric Lefkofsky's decision to build Tempus after his wife's cancer diagnosis gives the company a Just Cause that is personal, specific, and validated by years of execution. The company's willingness to sustain hundreds of millions in losses while building its data platform and diagnostic capabilities reflects long-term investment over short-term earnings optimization. However, the company is still young (11 years), has not been tested through a major crisis or leadership transition, and its competitive language occasionally focuses on market capture rather than self-improvement.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Tempus was born from Eric Lefkofsky's personal experience with his wife's breast cancer diagnosis, creating a founding story that is resilient, inclusive, service-oriented, and idealistic — closely matching Sinek's criteria for a Just Cause [3][4]. The mission to make precision medicine accessible and to ensure every patient benefits from the data of all patients who came before them is both specific and bigger than any single product. Strategic decisions trace back to this purpose: building the world's largest clinical-molecular data library, expanding from oncology to cardiology and neuropsychiatry, and pursuing the Personalis acquisition to broaden testing capabilities. However, Tempus is only 11 years old and has not yet been tested through a major crisis or leadership transition, which prevents a score of 3.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Tempus has grown to 3,800 employees and attracted partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies (AstraZeneca, GSK, Merck, Recursion), suggesting a competent and motivated workforce [4]. The company's Investor Day and recruitment of talent from both healthcare and technology sectors reflect organizational ambition. However, no specific evidence of exceptional organizational trust — voluntary turnover data, employee empowerment programs, or cultural practices that create psychological safety — was found. As a high-growth company, Tempus is likely in a dynamic but potentially stressful organizational phase.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Tempus collaborates extensively with potential competitors and complementary players — strategic partnerships with AstraZeneca, GSK, Merck, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals demonstrate a collaborative rather than adversarial competitive posture [4]. The Personalis acquisition represents a willingness to bring in external capabilities rather than insisting on building everything internally. Management positions Tempus as advancing precision medicine rather than defeating specific competitors, framing the opportunity as expanding the market rather than capturing share.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Tempus has expanded significantly from its original oncology diagnostics focus into cardiology, neuropsychiatry (pharmacogenomics via the nP assay), inherited disease testing (Ambry acquisition), and biopharma data licensing [4]. The company has also evolved its revenue model from pure diagnostics to a data platform business where the Insights and Trials products represent high-margin recurring revenue. These expansions demonstrate meaningful strategic evolution, though they are extensions of the original data-and-diagnostics model rather than transformative reinventions of the business.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Tempus sustained cumulative net losses of over $1.4B through 2025 while building its data platform and diagnostic capabilities, demonstrating willingness to invest heavily in long-term capability over short-term profitability [4]. The $1.5-1.7B Personalis acquisition while the company had only just reached quarterly profitability represents a bold bet on expanding capabilities. However, much of this investment was funded by investor capital rather than sacrificing established earnings, and the company has not yet faced a situation requiring costly trade-offs between profitable existing businesses and cause-driven new directions.

investment_thesis: Tempus AI at $66.75 with a $12.0B market cap is the leading AI-powered precision medicine platform, achieving a critical inflection point with its first quarter of net profitability ($5.6M) in Q2 2026 on $382.5M revenue (+22% YoY) [1][2]. The Diagnostics segment delivered 31% oncology volume growth while Data & Applications grew 28%, and adjusted EBITDA of $8.0M (up 244% YoY) validates the path to sustained profitability with full-year guidance of ~$65M EBITDA on $1.595-1.605B revenue [2]. The company sits at the intersection of two powerful secular trends — AI adoption and personalized healthcare — with a proprietary moat in the world's largest clinical-molecular data library that deepens with every test processed. The $1.5-1.7B Personalis acquisition expands into MRD testing and whole genome sequencing, and the $820.7M cash position provides ample runway [2].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on valuation risk and execution challenges. At $12B market cap on $1.43B TTM revenue with only $5.6M in quarterly net income, Tempus trades at approximately 8.4x revenue — a premium that requires sustained 20%+ growth and meaningful margin expansion to justify [1]. D/E of 324.6% reflects $1.17B in convertible notes that could dilute equity holders upon conversion, and the Personalis acquisition at $1.5-1.7B adds integration risk while the company is just reaching profitability [2][5]. ROE of -67.4% and cumulative losses exceeding $1.4B mean the balance sheet remains fragile despite cash reserves. CEO Lefkofsky's insider sales, while routine under 10b5-1 plans, are directionally negative at a critical valuation juncture [3]. The precision medicine market faces reimbursement uncertainty as payers scrutinize the cost-effectiveness of comprehensive genomic profiling, and competitor Guardant Health and established lab companies (Quest, LabCorp) are investing heavily in AI-powered diagnostics. Tempus must execute flawlessly on the Personalis integration while simultaneously scaling toward cash flow positivity — a challenging dual mandate [2][5].
key_catalysts: Profitability inflection — Q2 2026 net income of $5.6M marks the first profitable quarter, with $65M full-year EBITDA guidance and positive cash flow expected by year-end 2026, validating the long-term unit economics of the AI precision medicine platform [1][2]

Personalis acquisition ($1.5-1.7B) expanding into MRD testing and whole genome sequencing, expected to close late 2026 or early 2027, creating the most comprehensive genomics testing and AI analytics platform in healthcare [2]

Diagnostics volume growth of 31% YoY in oncology with Data & Applications revenue growing 28% — the flywheel of more tests generating more data generating more biopharma licensing revenue is accelerating [1][2]
key_risks: Premium valuation at ~8.4x TTM revenue with only nascent profitability leaves minimal margin of safety — any deceleration in growth or delay in margin expansion could trigger significant multiple compression from the $12B market cap [1]

Balance sheet leverage with $1.17B in convertible senior notes and D/E of 324.6% creates dilution risk upon conversion and limits financial flexibility for the $1.5-1.7B Personalis acquisition integration [2][5]

Reimbursement and competitive risk as payers scrutinize comprehensive genomic profiling costs, while Guardant Health, Foundation Medicine (Roche), and traditional lab companies invest heavily in AI-powered precision medicine capabilities [4]
